sectionProgressions.progression: F# - G - D - A - Bm - F# - G - D
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: V - VI - III - VII - i - V - VI - III
sectionProgressions.description: Neoclassical arpeggio riff outlining major and minor triads across the upper neck
Minimalist, bass-driven groove with light guitar texturing and harmonic feedback
Tension-building alternation between the subdominant and dominant chords

sectionProgressions.progression: G - D - F# - Bm - G - D - F# - Bm
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: VI - III - V - i - VI - III - V - i
sectionProgressions.description: Explosive wall-of-sound power chords supporting Bellamy's soaring operatic vocals
Violent oscillating fuzz feedback resolving on a crushing final B minor power chord

harmonicFunction: Starting on the dominant V (F#) immediately establishes classical tension before resolving to B minor
The A# note in F# major (derived from B Harmonic Minor) acts as an exotic leading tone
G (VI) to D (III) steps smoothly into the relative major sphere, providing anthemic lift
The chorus resolves triumphantly into Bm (i) on the third bar of each phrase

techniques.name: Neoclassical Triad Arpeggio Picking Across Strings 1-3
techniques.description: Matthew Bellamy's iconic introductory riff, demanding rapid, fluid alternate picking across the high E, B, and G strings with frequent position shifts.

notes: Use strict alternate picking (down-up-down-up) or light sweeping for string changes
Fret-hand fingers must maintain precise independence without collapsing
Shift positions cleanly between the 6th fret (A#), 7th fret (B), and 9th fret (C#)
Accent the highest note of each arpeggiated shape on the high E string
sequence: Ascend through F# major arpeggio: 6th fret high E, 7th fret B, 6th fret G
Shift to G major arpeggio at the 7th and 8th frets
Sweep down through D major arpeggio at the 10th and 11th frets
Descend through A and B minor shapes to complete the circular phrase
tips: Practice with a clean tone initially to expose any sloppy string muting or timing drift
Anchor the picking hand wrist gently on the bridge pins for maximum picking speed
Keep the pick angle slightly slanted to slice across the strings effortlessly

techniques.name: High-Gain Fuzz Articulation & Pitch Feedback Control
techniques.description: Utilizing an aggressive Germanium fuzz pedal (ZVex Fuzz Factory) to create velcro-like gating, searing harmonic sustain, and controlled pitch oscillation.

notes: Set fuzz gate tight enough to eliminate string hiss between staccato hits
Use guitar volume control to tame oscillation during rhythm passages
Manipulate guitar proximity to amplifier speakers for musical feedback singing
Execute staccato power chord mutes for crisp modern rock impact
sequence: Strike high-register opening notes with full fuzz saturation
Mute all strings with both hands on beat 4 for an immediate silence gate
Open up power chords during the chorus with sustained fuzz rumble
Tilt guitar toward amplifier during the outro to generate screaming harmonic sirens
tips: Ensure fresh batteries or clean isolated power for the Fuzz Factory
Use the bridge humbucker for maximum bite and feedback harmonic sensitivity
Keep left-hand muting vigilant to prevent unwanted runaway screeching

sections.name: Sweeping B Harmonic Minor Arpeggio Riff
sections.description: Ranked among the greatest guitar riffs of the 21st century—a tour-de-force of neoclassical arpeggio sweeps, Bach-like counterpoint, and searing fuzz tone.
notes: Play across strings 1, 2, and 3 using strict alternate picking at 136 BPM
Outlines F# major with the exotic A# leading tone on the 6th fret of string 1
Transitions seamlessly into G major and D major shapes across the neck
Recorded through a custom Manson guitar with an integrated ZVex Fuzz Factory

sections.name: Driving Bass-Driven Rhythm Verse
sections.description: Chris Wolstenholme's thunderous fuzz bass carries the groove, allowing Bellamy's guitar to interject with subtle feedback swells and harmonic accents.
notes: Guitar plays tasteful clean or volume-swelled stabs on offbeats
Let the bass drive the momentum while saving guitar energy for the chorus
Control guitar volume to suppress fuzz oscillation between vocal phrases

sections.name: Pre-Chorus Chromatic Lift
sections.description: Tension builds as the guitars enter with driving staccato power chords cycling between Em and F#.
notes: Tight palm-muted eighth notes building in volume and intensity
The F# chord introduces sharp harmonic minor tension right before the chorus explosion
Unmute completely on the final measure with an open pick slide

sections.name: Explosive Stadium Chorus
sections.description: The song erupts with crushing wall-of-sound power chords supporting Bellamy's soaring operatic vocals: 'My plug in baby, crucifies my enemies...'
notes: Massive fuzz distortion across root-5th power chords
G5 (3rd fret low E) to D5 (5th fret A string) provides anthemic major lift
F#5 pulls into B5 with heavy classical authority
Keep right hand loose and powerful with full arm strumming motions

sections.name: Riff Recapitulation & Extended Solo Flourish
sections.description: The signature intro riff returns with additional improvisational embellishments, octave jumps, and whammy pitch manipulation.
notes: Execute the arpeggio riff with even greater velocity and swagger
Dig in with the pick to induce harmonic squeals on the high notes
Climb into the 14th-17th fret register on the final turnaround

sections.name: Feedback Siren Outro Climax
sections.description: Bellamy lets his guitar scream with self-oscillating pitch feedback, sliding up the neck before slamming into a final, ringing B5 power chord.
notes: Manipulate guitar volume and proximity to the amp for wild sirens
Pick scrapes and whammy dives adding explosive chaos
Concludes on a decisive, heavily gated B5 power chord ring-out

guitar.recommended: Manson Custom Electric with built-in ZVex Fuzz Factory
guitar.pickup: Hot bridge humbucker (Seymour Duncan JB or Manson MBK-2) for aggressive punch

amp.recommended: Marshall JCM2000 DSL100 or Marshall JCM800

effects.distortion: ZVex Fuzz Factory (Gate 7.0, Comp 5.0, Drive 8.0, Stab 8.0) for gated velcro fuzz
effects.other: DigiTech Whammy 4 for octave shifts and pitch glides

beginner.title: Chorus Power Chords & 136 BPM Rhythm
steps: Master the G5, D5, F#5, and B5 root-5th power chord fingerings
Practice shifting cleanly between frets 2, 3, 5, and 7 on the lower strings
Work with a metronome at 100 BPM playing steady eighth-note downstrokes
Gradually build stamina up to the recording tempo of 136 BPM

intermediate.title: Arpeggio Shape Navigation at Half Speed
steps: Isolate the F# and G major arpeggio fingerings on strings 1, 2, and 3
Practice strict alternate picking (down-up-down-up) at 80 BPM
Coordinate the fret-hand position shifts between frets 6, 7, and 10
Incorporate the pre-chorus staccato power chord dynamics

advanced.title: The Full 136 BPM Intro Riff & Fuzz Control
steps: Play the complete introductory arpeggio riff up to full speed with zero hesitation
Dial in an aggressive, gated fuzz tone stack without unwanted screeching
Execute the high-register solo flourishes in the recapitulation section
Perform the entire song with authentic alternative rock power and swagger

commonMistakes: Collapsing into hammer-ons and pull-offs instead of cleanly alternate-picking the intro arpeggios
Rushing the tempo during the F# to G arpeggio position shift
Letting the Fuzz Factory oscillate out of control during quiet verse passages
Hitting unmuted adjacent strings during high-speed picking on strings 1, 2, and 3
practiceRoutine: 5 mins: Right-hand alternate picking synchronization warm-up with metronome
10 mins: Slow, isolated practice on the F# major arpeggio shape at 90 BPM
10 mins: Drilling the position shift between G major (7th fret) and D major (10th fret)
15 mins: Playing the full intro riff incrementally from 100 BPM to 136 BPM
10 mins: Power chord chorus stamina drills with heavy pick attack
focusAreas: Strict alternate picking mechanics on high strings
Fret-hand finger independence and arched fingertips
Fuzz pedal gate and noise control with guitar volume knob
Endurance and rhythmic pocket at 136 BPM
metronomeWork: Start intro riff at 80 BPM, increasing in 5 BPM increments only after 3 flawless runs
Practice chorus downstrokes at 140 BPM (slightly faster than record) to build reserve stamina
Drill pre-chorus staccato stops with click on beats 2 and 4
